top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces and aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, Ormco, Spark, Lightforce, KLOwen, self-ligating braces, twin brackets, SmartSTL, Angel, ClearCorrect, Suresmile
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, time saving, visit reduction, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, practice optimisation, staff efficiency, diary changes, emergencies decrease, adaptive aligner change, average visit reduction, efficiency in bracket systems, rentability
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM actually saves time or money, reduces appointments, or improves practice profitability. Some are skeptical that DM adds value for braces, not just aligners, or that the workflow changes are worth the investment.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, white paper, peer-reviewed, recent studies, only German studies, only Australian studies, European sources, US doctors
sample_queries: How much chair time reduction achieved
Show how can doctors increases the profitability if their practices using DM
How can I make DM work in a practice with 8 chairs and 15 assistants in a way that they really get the real benefits and make it work financially as well in The Netherlands?
Are Damon brackets more efficient than other brands?
Could you provide any data demonstrating improved patient compliance with DM or its impact on patient outcomes
top_needs.gap_assessment: Direct, high-quality comparative studies quantifying ROI, chair time, and appointment reduction for both braces and aligners are limited, especially by region and bracket type. More robust, region-specific economic analyses and workflow impact studies are needed.

top_needs.title: Accuracy and reliability of DM’s AI and SmartSTL for clinical monitoring and diagnostics
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, reliability, accuracy of SmartSTL, FDA class I, occlusal assessment, accuracy of scanning, AI vs orthodontist, passivity detection, refinement fit
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are skeptical about whether the AI is as accurate as a human, can reliably detect clinical changes, or is safe for diagnostic use. Some express distrust or fear of AI replacing clinical judgment.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, white paper, clinical study, peer-reviewed, only academic publication
sample_queries: Information on the accuracy of DM, a patient has questioned the ability of the AI to detect clinical observations
Specificity and sensitivity results for FDA application

Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
Looking for white papers on Smart STL accuracy to help convince a doctor to use it in the practice.
How accurate is DentalMonitorings AI and will it save me money
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for more peer-reviewed, head-to-head studies comparing DM’s AI and SmartSTL accuracy to orthodontists and other digital tools, especially for specific clinical tasks and regulatory benchmarks.

top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether patients actually like using DM, if it improves compliance, or if it adds complexity or dissatisfaction. Some want proof that DM differentiates their practice or improves staff morale.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, peer-reviewed, insights, university studies

top_needs.title: Reduction in aligner refinements and improved tracking with DM remote monitoring
top_needs.metrics_sought: refinement reduction, nontracking aligners, aligner unseat tracking, unfinished aligner sets, fitting and tracking quality
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are skeptical that DM actually reduces the number of refinements or improves aligner tracking, and want to see comparative data between brands and with/without DM.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, retrospective cohort study, data analysis
sample_queries: I am looking for fitting and tacking quality between different aligner brands. Specifically Spark, Angel, Invisalign, clearcorrect and suresmile

number of refinements for monitored patients, nontracking aligners, no-Go influence, unfinished aligner sets

top_needs.gap_assessment: Direct comparative studies on refinement rates and tracking outcomes across aligner brands with and without DM are sparse. More robust, brand-specific, and multi-center data are needed.
